back: A named block of statements that performs a task when called with CALL; it does not return a value.
A named block that returns one value with RETURN; it is called inside an expression.
Parameter: the variable in the routine's header. Argument: the actual value supplied in the call.
The routine gets a copy; changes inside do not affect the original variable.
The routine works on the original variable; changes inside change it. Used with procedures.
PROCEDURE Name(P : TYPE) ... ENDPROCEDURE; FUNCTION Name(P : TYPE) RETURNS TYPE ... ENDFUNCTION; CALL Name(args).
Local: exists only inside the routine. Global: available everywhere, but avoid changing it inside routines.
Reuse, easier testing and maintenance, shorter main program, work shared between programmers.
Numbers and strings cannot be changed through a parameter: return the value, or pass a list.
